videos.script:
The planner is one long page. {{page}} Today it becomes a page and four small components, and the question is how they talk.

The default is simple. {{down}} Values go down as props. When a child wants something to change, it calls a function its parent gave it. The parent decides.

Then binding. {{bind}} A form field bound to a variable shows it, and typing changes it. One attribute, both directions. The planner gets a real form for adding a session.

Then a trap. {{trap}} A child that changes its parent's state directly. It works. Nothing complains. And it quietly takes a decision away from the page that owns it.

Then the exception done properly. {{bindable}} A component can offer a binding of its own, with bindable. You will see when that is the right choice, and the silent failure when it is missing.

And last, styles. {{styles}} A style block in a component applies to that component and nothing else. The compiler even tells you when a rule can never match.
